parts.title: Part 1 — Introduction and interview
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask general questions about yourself and a few familiar topics. Answer naturally and try to extend each answer with a reason or example. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Let's talk about travelling. Do you like to travel?
What is your favourite means of transport?
Did you travel much when you were a child?
Now let's talk about technology. How much time do you spend using technology every day?
What technology do you use most often?
Has technology changed the way you communicate with friends and family?
Let's move on to shopping. Do you prefer shopping online or in physical stores?
When was the last time you bought something online?
Do you enjoy shopping, or do you find it stressful?

parts.title: Part 2 — Individual long turn
parts.instructions: You will be given a topic card. You have one minute to prepare and may make notes. Then speak for one to two minutes. Try to keep talking until the examiner stops you.
parts.cue_card_topic: Describe a memorable trip you have taken.
cue_card_bullets: and explain why the trip was memorable

questions.question: Would you like to go back to this place again in the future?

parts.title: Part 3 — Two-way discussion
parts.instructions: The examiner will ask further questions connected to the Part 2 topic. These are more abstract and require you to explain, compare, and speculate. Try to give extended, well-reasoned answers. This part lasts 4–5 minutes.

questions.question: Why do many people enjoy travelling to other countries?
What are the advantages and disadvantages of tourism for local communities?
Some people think tourism damages local culture more than it benefits it. Do you agree?
How has technology changed the way people plan and experience travel?
Do you think international travel will become easier or more difficult in the future?
Should governments limit the number of tourists visiting popular destinations? Why or why not?
